- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.9) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid immediate peak overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often fails to correct downward; apply a downward bias of 5–10% for 3–5 subsequent periods.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if 30d forecast mean is >85, true outcome typically drops below 75–78; adjust for downward drift if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., -1.98, -0.51, 0.24), model tends to ignore trend; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
